lines.text: You can trade gold, oil, or Tesla without ever owning any of it. It's called a CFD.
CFD means contract for difference. You and the broker make a deal: whoever the price moves against pays the other the difference.
Think the price will rise? Go long. It climbs ten dollars, the broker pays you ten.
Think it will fall? Go short. It drops ten, you get paid ten. Falling markets become a chance too.
Now the hook: leverage. To open a thousand dollar position, you might only put down fifty. That's called margin.
So a five percent move up doubles your fifty. But a five percent move down wipes it out.
When your losses eat your margin, the broker closes you out automatically. That's a margin call.
And it's never free. You pay the spread to get in, and a fee for every night you hold.
Why do people love it? Small money, big exposure, and you can bet on either direction.
But here's the truth: brokers in Europe must publish how many clients lose money. It's usually over seventy percent.
Not financial advice. If you try it, use small leverage, and always set a stop.
Send this to a friend on Orbi Transfer. Now you know!
